output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. Agents' in-call credit limit dropped from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. Referrals on billing calls rose from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, against 82% for the rest. Billing FCR fell from 79% to 56%. Referral rates are about the same across tenure bands (53–56%). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount (75% to about 67%). The April intake is only slightly lower, at 66.4%. Tariff enquiries are a bigger share of calls but still resolve at 85%. I can't rule out a small IVR effect, and I haven't established how much of the rise in complaints comes from the FCR fall. Don't put the April intake on performance plans: it would punish the wrong group. Run the credit-authority trial from Finance's own condition: a higher limit on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Don't restore the limit everywhere at once. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. MI can add referral breakdowns within a day, so the three-month dashboard rebuild isn't needed now. Confidence is fairly high.
